verdict.rationale: Hands-on community reports say Ghostty handles heavy output well: catting a large file puts it 'in the same league as Alacritty and Ptyxis', and users call it a 'modern high performance terminal'. However, nothing in the pack documents GPU-accelerated rendering. Responsiveness evidence is mixed, with users reporting noticeable input lag and a newer benchmark showing ~13ms average latency. missing for 10: first-party documentation of GPU-accelerated rendering (e.g. Metal/OpenGL renderer), official throughput/latency benchmarks, consistent evidence of low input latency under load

support.subject: As a developer, I can rely on GPU-accelerated rendering that stays fast and responsive under heavy output

citations.quote: On throughput (catting a large file), Ghostty performs very well, among the same league as Alacritty and Ptyxis.
it's great to have another modern high performance terminal as an option for macOS and Linux.
For example, Neovim uses synchronized rendering to prevent tearing between frames.
